nodes.name: BoomTest.java
nodes.summary: Defines a JUnit test that always throws, producing an errors-only test class for Maven failure-output capture.

nodes.name: CalcTest.java
nodes.summary: Defines two deliberately failing JUnit cases and one passing calculator case so Maven output includes multiple failure blocks in one class.

nodes.name: grep_context_test.rs
nodes.summary: Verifies RTK grep context behavior for before and after lines, group separators, count and only-matching formats, and NUL-free output.

nodes.name: grep_faithful_format_test.rs
nodes.summary: Compares RTK grep output with native grep across recursive, filename, line-number, regex, context, colon-heavy, case, inversion, and piped-input cases.

nodes.name: guard_integration_test.rs
nodes.summary: Exercises the output-bloat guard and compact Git behaviors, ensuring useful compression remains enabled while tiny or failing commands preserve native signal and exit status.

nodes.name: pipeline_stdin_test.rs
nodes.summary: Validates that RTK's wc wrapper consumes piped standard input and preserves native failure exit codes.

nodes.name: search_compress_test.rs
nodes.summary: Tests search compression, contextual output, result caps, token reduction, flag handling, file clustering, binary detection, and true no-match status.

nodes.name: search_error_test.rs
nodes.summary: Ensures grep and ripgrep surface missing-file, invalid-regex, and partial-result errors with correct exit codes instead of silently reporting no matches.

nodes.name: search_faithful_test.rs
nodes.summary: Verifies that RTK preserves native grep and ripgrep dialects, ignore behavior, globbing, stdin streaming, passthrough modes, file listings, and regex-error semantics while still compressing bulky results.

layers.description: Process execution, guarded arguments, streaming and tee paths, truncation, telemetry, shared filtering, and parser formatting primitives.

layers.description: Runtime hook management and packaged integrations for Claude, Cursor, Copilot, Hermes, OpenCode, Pi, and OpenClaw environments.

layers.description: Rust integration tests, hook plugin tests, shell test drivers, and captured cross-tool fixtures that verify faithful compression and failures.

tour.title: What RTK Solves
tour.description: Start with the README to understand RTK as a proxy that reduces token-heavy command output while preserving useful signal. Its installation, supported-command, configuration, telemetry, and savings guidance establishes the user contract that every later module implements.

tour.title: CLI Entry and Dispatch
tour.description: With that contract established, main.rs shows how the Clap CLI receives both RTK meta commands and proxied tool invocations. Its dispatch logic routes supported commands into filters while validating the fallback to native executables, making this the earliest code-level map of runtime behavior.

tour.title: Command Filter Families
tour.description: The entry point fans out through cmds/mod.rs into ecosystem families for cloud, Git, JavaScript, and general system tools. These module boundaries organize a wide command surface without changing the common proxy model introduced in Step 2, so learn the family map before individual adapters.

tour.title: Shared Execution Core
tour.description: Those command families converge on the shared core: runner.rs defines captured, streamed, exit-aware, and passthrough execution, while args_utils.rs restores wrapped command boundaries. core/mod.rs exposes the infrastructure, and guard.rs enforces the never-worse invariant by rejecting filtered output that would cost more tokens than raw output.

tour.title: Streaming and Recovery
tour.description: Building on the runner, stream.rs owns bounded capture, concurrent pipe draining, and line or block filtering, while tee.rs preserves raw output for recovery. truncate.rs applies consistent caps and tracking.rs records command-level savings and parse failures, completing the output lifecycle from process launch to observable result.
tour.languageLesson: Rust traits provide separate line- and block-filter interfaces, allowing the streaming engine to accept different filtering behaviors behind one execution contract.

tour.title: Declarative Filter Pipeline
tour.description: After capture, toml_filter.rs loads, validates, compiles, tests, and applies declarative regex pipelines with built-in, user, and project precedence. The filter authoring guide defines that contract, gcc.toml shows how noise is removed without losing diagnostics, and .rtk/filters.toml exposes safe project overrides.

tour.title: Specialized Command Adapters
tour.description: When TOML rules are not expressive enough, specialized Rust adapters encode command-aware behavior. The AWS, Git, pnpm, Cargo, and search handlers demonstrate structured parsing, subcommand dispatch, streaming or buffering choices, guarded compaction, preserved failures, and raw-output recovery across very different tools.

tour.title: Canonical Parser Model
tour.description: Several specialized adapters normalize tool-specific results through the shared parser layer. parser/types.rs defines serializable canonical test and dependency models, parser/mod.rs defines degradation and recovery behavior, and formatter.rs renders bounded compact, verbose, or ultra output.
tour.languageLesson: Serializable Rust structs create a canonical intermediate representation: tool-specific parsers populate shared result types, and formatters render them at different verbosity levels.

tour.title: Secure Hook Lifecycle
tour.description: With filtering and execution understood, the hook layer explains how coding agents invoke RTK before shell tools run. hook_cmd.rs and rewrite_cmd.rs turn permission-aware decisions into protocol responses, init.rs manages atomic installation and migration, and trust.rs prevents changed local filters from executing without review.

tour.title: Agent Integration Adapters
tour.description: The core hook decisions are adapted to each host by small integration shims. Claude and Cursor use shell protocols, OpenCode and Pi use TypeScript hooks, and OpenClaw adds denial and approval-required outcomes; all preserve the original command when RTK is unavailable or a rewrite fails.

tour.title: Behavioral Regression Contracts
tour.description: The integration and execution invariants are protected by tests that compare RTK with native behavior rather than only checking formatting helpers. The guard suite catches output-bloat and exit-code regressions, search suites cover faithful dialects and real errors, and Claude and Hermes hook suites verify rewriting, pass-through, payload, timeout, and installation behavior.

tour.title: Build and Delivery Gates
tour.description: Finally, Cargo.toml fixes the crate, lint, optimized-build, and packaging contract, while scripts/test-all.sh exercises the assembled CLI and integrations. CI adds formatting, clippy, multi-platform, security, benchmark, and test gates; the release workflow builds and publishes cross-platform artifacts, and the architecture guide preserves the complete lifecycle for maintainers.
